notes.title: Anchor, pick up a mooring, spend the night
items: X stops the boat. Slow down first: under 2 kt she lets go her anchor in up to 25 m of water. Near a mooring or a dock (Ayala Cove, Sam's, Sausalito, Pier 39, Horseshoe Cove) and under 2.5 kt, X picks up the buoy or brings her alongside.
While she is held the sails are stowed, the cover is on the boom, and you can see her rode or mooring line. She swings to the wind and the tide.
X again gets her under way, on the tack with more water ahead.

Z turns in for the night when you are alone on the water. You wake at 06:30 to the next morning's wind and tide, and the night goes in your logbook. She will not let you sleep in a gale or where she would touch bottom at low water.
Other boats see what you are doing: at anchor, on a mooring, alongside.

notes.title: Racing, and a wind tunnel for your sails
items: Racing. Press R, pick a course and the minutes to the gun, and call it. Everyone on the water is told and can join. Raccoon Strait to McCovey Cove, Round Alcatraz, the Golden Gate dash, or the route on your own chart.
Pace boats. Up to three boats sailed by the autopilot race with you, in the same boat as yours, each a little off the pace. Race them alone or alongside your friends.
A countdown under the clock, the course on your chart, live places while you race, and your time at the finish. Races and wins go in your logbook.
Who is out. The same panel lists every boat on the water with you: skipper, boat, what she is doing, and her range and bearing.
Wind tunnel, suggested by Scott. Press F to see the air over your sails: smooth where it follows the sail, red and broken where a sail is sheeted too hard, grey and shaking where it luffs.
The wind tunnel card also tells you the wind angle your sails, as set, are asking for: steer to the sails, or trim to the course.
Keys. The board (B) now has a page listing every control.
The roadmap is now a board: sprint columns across, lanes for sailing experience, multiplayer, places, platform and progression. Filter by lane, and the most wanted cards rise to the top.

notes.title: Gust warnings and release notes
items: Gust warnings. The readout shows a gust on its way and how long until it reaches you, and says when you are in one. A strong one raises an alert and drops time back to real speed so you can ease the main.
What's new. This page. A marker on the Roadmap link tells you when there is something you have not read.
The recorded weather runs for 36 hours. When a boat reaches the end, the same day now starts over instead of freezing in the dark.
A boat left running for days no longer drags everyone who joins into her clock.

notes.title: Roadmap, feedback and coaching
items: Roadmap. Press B to see what is planned, in releases, and vote things up or down.
Feedback. Tell us what you think or report a problem without leaving the boat. It can attach what the boat was doing at the time.
Point of sail. The readout now names it: close-hauled, beam reach, running, in irons, and which tack you are on.
Coaching hints. If a sail has been luffing or stalled for a while, or you are stuck in irons, one line says what to do. C turns them off.
Hail other boats with Enter. Their words show on your screen.
Places to meet on the chart: McCovey Cove, Ayala Cove, Sam's in Tiburon and more. Click one to add it to your route.
A logbook of your miles, hours and marks, and the fleet's.
Fixed: a boat could come back broken after the game updated under her, and then would not start again.

notes.title: Real 3 km wind, a choice of when to cast off, knockdowns
items: The wind is now NOAA's 3 km HRRR model for 14 July 2024. It builds through the day, funnels through the Gate and shifts the way it did.
Gusts and lulls sized from the model's own gust speeds.
Choose when to cast off: a light morning, the afternoon sea breeze, or the evening as it eases.
Crash gybes. Let the boom fly across in a breeze with the main out and she can be knocked flat.

notes.title: Regatta
items: A new name, and a join screen: where to sail, an optional first lesson, then your boat.
Three boats: a 30 ft sloop, a 38 and a 45 ft performance cruiser. Name her and choose her colours.

notes.title: Autopilot, traffic and sailing in company
items: An autopilot that holds a heading, a wind angle or your route, with the crew trimming.
Ferries, ships and other boats on the Bay, and more of the shore.
Open the same link as a friend and you are on the same water.

notes.title: The Bay, the chart and the crew
items: San Francisco Bay with NOAA's tidal stream, tide and depths.
A chartplotter with waypoints, leg times, plan against actual and the forecast.
A wind and tide dial, and crew aboard.
